title: Boniface and the oak
hookLine: an English monk to the Germans, remembered for felling a sacred oak and dying a martyr

lines: AN AXE IN A SACRED OAK.
cards: An axe bites into an enormous oak in a clearing in Hesse, in what is now Germany. The tree is sacred to the people who live here; the account calls it the oak of Jupiter, giving their god a Roman name.
A crowd has gathered, cursing the man with the axe. He's a monk from England named Boniface, and the local Christians have urged him on. He makes one cut.
Then, says the account, a great wind from above shakes the tree, and it comes crashing down.

teach.h: A MONK FROM ENGLAND, ACROSS THE SEA.
teach.b: Our main source is a life of Boniface written by a priest named Willibald. Boniface was born in England, became a monk, and left a settled life to preach among the Germanic peoples across the sea.
The oak is the scene his story turns on.
In Willibald's telling, the people who had cursed him saw the tree fall and began to praise God instead, and Boniface used the timber to build a small chapel dedicated to Saint Peter.
The wood of the old shrine became the walls of the new one. Now the honest part. It was someone's holy tree.
The people in that clearing weren't villains in their own story, and Christians have disagreed about how to meet another people's sacred places.

Earlier on this path, Pope Gregory advised the missionaries in England to keep the old temples and take out only the idols: bless, don't destroy. Boniface's story goes the other way. Both are part of the church's story.
Then the ending. As an old man, Boniface went to preach in Frisia, near the North Sea. At dawn one morning his camp was attacked.
Willibald says his companions reached for weapons, and Boniface stopped them: scripture, he told them, teaches us not to repay evil for evil.

In the King James words of Paul to the Romans: "Recompense to no man evil for evil." He was killed there with his companions. Tradition adds that he held a book of the gospels over his head as the blow fell.
The man remembered for an axe died refusing a sword.

teach.h: RECOMPENSE TO NO MAN EVIL FOR EVIL.
teach.b: Christians honor him as a martyr and an apostle to the Germans.

how: Boniface is honored as a saint and martyr, especially in Germany and the Netherlands; Catholic, Anglican and Lutheran churches remember him on his feast day, and his tomb is kept at Fulda.

Willibald says he stopped his companions from fighting back.

games.q: you're Boniface, an old man in Frisia. your camp is attacked at dawn, and your companions reach for weapons. what do you tell them?
o: put the weapons down. do not repay evil for evil.
games.why: Willibald says Boniface forbade them to fight, citing scripture. the man of the axe died refusing a sword.

practice: Christians reserve worship for God, but anything can quietly take that place: a phone, a bank balance, someone's approval, being right, being busy. Name, in a word, what has grown too big for you, without fixing it yet.
If you pray, hand that word to God and ask for help cutting it down to size; if you don't, notice how much room it takes up.
